claim: Roman's Solar Array Sun Shield is designed to continuously face the Sun while supplying about 4.1 kW at Sun-Earth L2, making orientation geometry an explicit power-system service in a current mission.

provenance.source_title: Telescope Milestone: Teams Check Out NASA Roman Solar Panels
limitations: Roman is macroscale and cannot establish 10 mm SNS control feasibility.
The source does not quantify the incremental mass or power cost of Sun-facing control for SNS-like nodes.
provenance.fact_summary: NASA states Roman's six-panel solar-array sun-shield will continuously face the Sun and provide about 4.1 kW.
provenance.inference_summary: Hosted SNS comparisons should continue to charge orientation and geometry maintenance rather than treating sunward pointing as free.
provenance.speculation_summary: Future SNS host platforms may provide sunward geometry as a shared service if the system-level mass and energy trade closes.
